Detailed User Journey Map

An end-to-end view of sponsorship, beneficiary decision-making, registration intake, official payment, PRC handoff, confirmation, claims readiness, and renewal.

Status

Primary journey

Updated
4 Sep 2026

◆
Scope reconciliation used in this map The committed sprint backlog includes the landing page, benefit storyboard, referral QR/link, application intake, privacy checkpoint, pilot data store, protected admin access/export, and confirmation/recovery states. Two conflicts are resolved using the latest project decisions: GCash integration is conditional, so the MVP uses an official PRC payment handoff; and PRC must store all registration and payment data, so a proposed pilot store may contain real data only if PRC controls or explicitly approves the architecture and retention. Otherwise it is transient/synthetic-only. Direct PRC API integration, advanced analytics, and loyalty mechanics remain deferred.

End-to-end view

One journey, five actors, nine stages

The sponsor initiates and funds; the household helper learns, decides, and owns their information; the platform guides and records; the project admin handles first-line operations; PRC approves, stores official records, confirms membership, and handles official program or claims matters.

Journey map

Detailed stages

Each stage connects visible actions to backstage ownership, emotional state, failure recovery, product requirements, and measurable evidence.

01

Sponsor preparation

Understand the offer and prepare a respectful, fundable sponsorship.

Committed MVP
Primary actorStudent sponsor
TriggerSchool/PRC-approved campaign
Emotional stateCurious, slightly cautious
Exit stateReady to invite responsibly

Sponsor

  • Opens campaign or referral page.
  • Reads purpose, price, benefits, and limits.
  • Checks whether parent/guardian support is needed.
  • Selects a known potential beneficiary.

Beneficiary

No data or commitment yet. The person should not be pre-enrolled.

Platform

  • Shows mobile-first Tagalog/English overview.
  • Displays PRC-approved content status and review date.
  • Explains sponsorship vs. membership.
  • Provides sponsor conduct guidance.

Project admin

  • Publishes only approved campaign content.
  • Provides first-line FAQs.
  • Monitors aggregate landing-page use.

PRC

  • Approves facts, branding, and official routes.
  • Provides current program contacts and terms.

Pain points

  • Student does not want to sound like a salesperson.
  • Program may be confused with commercial insurance.
  • Minor payment rules are unclear.

Design opportunities

  • Use a 60-second sponsor briefing and comprehension check.
  • Provide a respectful invitation script.
  • Show “what you can and cannot see.”

Recovery

  • If approval or payment rules are unresolved, save a draft—not an invitation.
  • Route questions to the named project admin.

Requirements and controls

Content owner, source, review date, and PRC approval state; no beneficiary personal data; clear voluntary-participation guidance; low-bandwidth page; parent/guardian notice where required.

Success evidence

≥80% sponsor comprehension

Sponsor can accurately explain purpose, cost, main benefits, limits, and the beneficiary’s right to decline.

02

Explain and invite

Make a personal offer without collecting unnecessary information or applying pressure.

Committed MVP
Primary actorsSponsor + beneficiary
TouchpointQR, link, or in-person handoff
Emotional stateAwkward / suspicious
Exit stateInvitation viewed privately

Sponsor

  • Shares a private QR or link.
  • Explains that sponsorship is voluntary.
  • Offers assistance without taking over.
  • Steps away so the beneficiary can review privately.

Beneficiary

  • Checks who sent the invitation.
  • Asks whether it is really connected to PRC.
  • Chooses language and opens the overview.
  • May defer or decline without consequence.

Platform

  • Validates referral attribution.
  • Shows sponsor identity only with permission.
  • Separates “learn more” from “agree.”
  • Supports invalid-link fallback.

Project admin

  • Issues and deactivates pilot referral links.
  • Investigates broken or misused codes.
  • Cannot see beneficiary details at this stage.

PRC

No operational action unless legitimacy or misuse is escalated.

Pain points

  • Scam fear and distrust of links.
  • Employer-family power imbalance.
  • Referral attribution may feel like tracking.

Design opportunities

  • Explain why the referral exists and what it records.
  • Use privacy-safe sponsor identification.
  • Provide official PRC contact verification.

Recovery

  • Invalid link loads the general landing page.
  • “Not now” exits without reminders unless requested.
  • Report-suspicious-link route goes to admin.

Requirements and controls

Unique pilot link/QR; nullable referral ID; transparent attribution notice; no public sponsor or beneficiary directory; invitation expiration; report/mute path; no enrollment created from a scan.

Success evidence

Invitation trust + privacy

Beneficiary can identify the sender and purpose and understands that opening the page creates no obligation.

03

Learn and decide

Turn program terms into plain-language understanding before any data collection.

Committed MVP
Primary actorBeneficiary
TouchpointsLanding page + storyboard + FAQ
Emotional stateSkeptical → informed
Exit stateChooses apply, pause, or decline

Sponsor

  • Answers only what the platform explains.
  • Does not promise claims outcomes.
  • Allows time for independent decision.

Beneficiary

  • Reads ₱1,200/year and who will pay.
  • Reviews benefit amounts and examples.
  • Checks exclusions and claims process.
  • Uses preferred language or asks for help.
  • Completes comprehension check.

Platform

  • Presents benefit cards and a household scenario.
  • Keeps exclusions next to relevant benefits.
  • Labels provisional or unapproved details.
  • Supports save/share/print without exposing data.

Project admin

  • Answers platform-navigation questions.
  • Escalates benefit or eligibility questions.
  • Tracks comprehension in aggregate.

PRC

  • Approves the content version.
  • Owns official interpretation of benefits, eligibility, and exclusions.

Pain points

  • Insurance or claims terminology is intimidating.
  • ₱100/month phrasing could imply a payment plan that is not approved.
  • Mobile data and time are limited.

Design opportunities

  • Grade-6-level Tagalog and short audio option.
  • Show annual amount prominently; use monthly equivalent only when approved.
  • Scenario → exact benefit → exact limitation.

Recovery

  • Save the learning state locally without personal data.
  • Offer PRC contact and in-person chapter option.
  • Let users return without repeated pressure.

Requirements and controls

Current fee, ages 3–85, benefit schedule, extended contexts, exclusions, claims deadlines, source/review date, content approval status, Tagalog/English first, accessible typography, optimized assets.

Success evidence

4 of 5 questions correct

Beneficiary can explain purpose, annual price, main benefits, important limits, and first claims step.

04

Agreement and application intake

Obtain informed agreement, collect only approved fields, and make errors recoverable.

Committed MVP
Primary actorBeneficiary
TouchpointsPrivacy notice + form + review
Emotional stateAnxious → in control
Exit stateConsented submission

Sponsor

  • May assist only after agreement.
  • Does not see identity or sensitive fields.
  • Does not check boxes for the beneficiary.

Beneficiary

  • Reads layered privacy notice.
  • Agrees or declines separately from payment.
  • Enters approved personal details.
  • Reviews and corrects before submission.
  • Receives a platform reference number.

Platform

  • Validates fields in plain language.
  • Captures agreement evidence and notice version for approved transfer to PRC-controlled storage.
  • Prevents duplicate retry.
  • Preserves unsent progress only under the approved retention design.
  • Creates visible success/error states.

Project admin

  • Views only authorized operational fields.
  • Supports technical errors.
  • Uses synthetic data if privacy gate is incomplete.

PRC

  • Approves fields, notice, lawful basis, and data handoff.
  • Receives official registration data.

Pain points

  • Fear of making a permanent mistake.
  • Shared phone or nearby sponsor reduces privacy.
  • Long address and identity fields are tiring.

Design opportunities

  • Explain why each field is needed.
  • Use short steps, review screen, and friendly Filipino errors.
  • Provide “continue privately” and save-and-resume.

Recovery

  • Network failure keeps form data locally and offers retry.
  • Duplicate protection avoids double submission.
  • Correction request goes to the approved PRC/admin route.

Requirements and controls

Explicit agreement when used as lawful basis; notice version and timestamp; PRC-approved fields; no real applicant data before privacy sign-off; encryption; shared-device protection; consent withdrawal/correction route; no data sent to external AI tools.

Success evidence

≤10 min beneficiary journey

100% of completed intake records contain approved agreement evidence or documented lawful basis; zero unresolved critical privacy defects.

05

Official sponsorship payment

Move money through an official PRC channel and define when a referral becomes a sponsorship.

MVP handoff · integration conditional
Primary actorSponsor / authorized payer
TouchpointOfficial PRC payment route
Emotional stateCautious → reassured
Exit statePayment received/reconcilable

Sponsor

  • Confirms beneficiary has agreed.
  • Uses PRC-approved GCash route or approved alternative.
  • Reviews amount and reference.
  • Keeps official receipt or proof.

Beneficiary

  • Sees who is paying and what the payment covers.
  • Is not asked to pay unless the arrangement changes.
  • Does not lose the right to withdraw merely because payment was attempted.

Platform

  • Links to official channel for MVP.
  • Preserves reference/referral IDs.
  • Shows “payment pending” until verified.
  • Does not store card, PIN, or wallet credentials.

Project admin

  • Reconciles minimum approved payment evidence.
  • Handles platform status mismatch.
  • Escalates refunds or payment disputes to PRC.

PRC

  • Owns official payment channel and receipt.
  • Confirms whether funds were received.
  • Owns refund and payment-dispute policy.

Pain points

  • GCash collaboration may not be ready.
  • Student may require adult payer approval.
  • Payment success may not return automatically.

Design opportunities

  • Use a clear external-payment interstitial.
  • Show exact payee, amount, and reference format.
  • Provide “I paid” reconciliation—not instant activation.

Recovery

  • Failed or abandoned payment returns to pending.
  • Duplicate or wrong-reference payment is escalated.
  • If the beneficiary declines, follow approved cancellation/refund rules.

Requirements and controls

Official channel only; final GCash/alternative decision; receipt owner; minor-payer rule; idempotent integrated payments if later added; reconciliation and refund process; never describe payment as consent or activation.

Success evidence

100% traceable payments

A referral is counted as a sponsorship only after sponsor-funded payment can be matched to the beneficiary’s registration.

06

PRC handoff and reconciliation

Transmit approved data, keep PRC as the source of truth, and surface exceptions.

Committed MVP · manual/secure export
Primary actorsProject admin + PRC
TouchpointsAdmin view, export, secure transfer
Emotional stateWaiting / operational focus
Exit statePRC received or needs attention

Sponsor

  • Sees high-level “submitted” or “needs attention.”
  • Does not see beneficiary fields or PRC notes.

Beneficiary

  • Receives reference and next-step expectations.
  • Provides corrections through approved route.

Platform

  • Displays only approved operational fields.
  • Persists real data only in PRC-controlled or formally approved storage; otherwise uses synthetic data.
  • Creates export/handoff manifest and audit event.
  • Tracks status without becoming the official record.

Project admin

  • Checks required fields and reference matches.
  • Exports in PRC-approved column order.
  • Transfers through approved secure method.
  • Logs PRC receipt and exceptions.

PRC

  • Receives and stores official registration/payment records.
  • Accepts, rejects, or asks for correction.
  • Returns authoritative membership status.

Pain points

  • No direct PRC API in Iteration 01.
  • CSV/manual transfer risks delay and version mismatch.
  • Platform and PRC statuses may diverge.

Design opportunities

  • Use an immutable handoff batch ID.
  • Show status owner and last-updated time.
  • Separate validation failure from PRC rejection.

Recovery

  • Rejected records enter “needs attention” with a safe correction request.
  • Duplicate batch detection prevents repeated handoff.
  • Mismatch report goes to PRC liaison.

Requirements and controls

Approved data map and storage owner; controller/processor roles; PRC-controlled or explicitly approved real-data persistence; retention/deletion; role-based security; individual admin credentials; batch reference; secure transfer; access removal at handover; auditable source-of-truth rule.

Success evidence

≥95% clean handoffs

Every exported record is either acknowledged by PRC or assigned a named next action; no unauthorized data exposure.

07

Membership verification and confirmation

Deliver durable proof and close the loop for both parties without exposing sensitive data.

Committed MVP · verification method open
Primary actorBeneficiary
TouchpointsConfirmation page + PRC message
Emotional stateImpatient → relieved
Exit stateVerified member with proof

Sponsor

  • Sees “completed” and payment receipt status.
  • Receives no Safe Card ID, health, or claims details unless explicitly authorized and necessary.

Beneficiary

  • Receives official membership confirmation.
  • Saves Safe Card ID and effective date.
  • Checks name/details and correction route.
  • Saves claims and emergency contacts.

Platform

  • Distinguishes platform submission from PRC verification.
  • Displays last-updated source and next action.
  • Provides printable/savable claims card.
  • May send SMS only if approved and in scope.

Project admin

  • Closes only after PRC verification evidence.
  • Handles missing platform notice.
  • Escalates missing official confirmation to PRC.

PRC

  • Issues authoritative Safe Card ID/effective date.
  • Owns activation and correction decisions.
  • Provides official support channels.

Pain points

  • Processing time is not yet approved.
  • Platform reference may be mistaken for membership ID.
  • SMS delivery may fail or be out of scope.

Design opportunities

  • Use distinct visual labels for “submitted” and “active.”
  • Offer screenshot/print and resend options.
  • Show who owns the next action.

Recovery

  • No promised turnaround until PRC approves one.
  • Missing confirmation creates a tracked escalation.
  • Wrong details route to official correction—not local edit.

Requirements and controls

Authoritative status source; clear platform vs. PRC reference; minimal sponsor-visible status; optional SMS decision; resend/accessibility alternatives; correction/escalation route; no unsupported “insured” or “activated” language.

Success evidence

≥70% completion in 7 days

Target applies only after PRC confirms the operational baseline. Beneficiary can locate proof and official contacts without help.

08

Membership use and claims readiness

Ensure the beneficiary knows what to do in an emergency or after an incident.

Education in MVP · claims handling by PRC
Primary actorBeneficiary/member
TouchpointsSaved guide + Hotline 143 + PRC claims
Emotional stateStressed → directed
Exit statePRC claim/support underway

Sponsor

  • May remind the member where official contacts are.
  • Does not receive claim status or medical details.

Beneficiary

  • For accident-related ambulance/blood emergency, calls 143 with member details.
  • Reports incident to PRC within 30 days.
  • Submits required documents within 60 days.
  • Uses PRC claims contacts for current requirements.

Platform

  • Shows approved emergency/claims guide.
  • Keeps source and review date visible.
  • Deep-links or calls official contacts.
  • Does not adjudicate or collect claim details.

Project admin

  • Supports access to the guide.
  • Immediately escalates benefit or claim questions to PRC.
  • Does not promise eligibility or outcome.

PRC

  • Provides emergency service and official claims instructions.
  • Receives documents.
  • Decides eligibility and claim outcome.

Pain points

  • High stress and little time during an emergency.
  • Member may not remember ID/effective date.
  • Detailed deadlines currently need final PRC confirmation.

Design opportunities

  • Create a one-screen offline-friendly emergency card.
  • Use “Call 143” as the primary emergency action.
  • Explain 30/60-day deadlines in simple timeline form.

Recovery

  • If the platform is unavailable, saved/printed PRC contacts remain usable.
  • Outdated content displays a warning and directs to PRC.
  • Claims disputes bypass project admin decision-making.

Requirements and controls

PRC-approved Hotline 143 wording; 30-day notice and 60-day documents guidance; official claims contacts; offline/screenshot format; no medical/claims collection; content expiry/review alert; clear disclaimer that PRC controls decisions.

Success evidence

First action identified

In testing, members can state who to contact, what information to keep, and the two time limits without asking the sponsor.

09

Renewal and responsible recognition

Support continuity without pressuring beneficiaries or turning people into public metrics.

Deferred / future option
Primary actorsBeneficiary + sponsor
TouchpointsPrivate reminder and renewal handoff
Emotional stateReflective / willing
Exit stateRenewed, declined, or expired

Sponsor

  • Receives a private reminder if appropriate.
  • Can offer another sponsorship without obligation.
  • May receive a private service milestone.

Beneficiary

  • Reviews updated terms and price.
  • Decides again; prior agreement is not assumed.
  • Can renew through official process or decline.

Platform

  • Uses opt-in, non-sensitive reminders.
  • Does not publicly rank recipients or disclose names.
  • Revalidates content before renewal.

Project admin

  • Monitors aggregate renewal interest.
  • Handles reminder preferences.
  • Escalates official renewal questions.

PRC

  • Confirms renewal eligibility and official terms.
  • Records renewed membership.

Pain points

  • Recognition can become competitive or coercive.
  • Contact preferences may change.
  • Terms may differ at renewal.

Design opportunities

  • Private recognition based on responsible actions, not volume alone.
  • Fresh education and agreement each year.
  • Simple opt-out and expiry status.

Recovery

  • No reminder without approved basis and preference.
  • Decline stops follow-up.
  • Expired membership is never displayed as active.

Requirements and controls

Not in Iteration 01. Before adding: PRC approval, reminder lawful basis, updated-content review, renewal-state model, non-coercive recognition policy, and clear opt-out.

Future success evidence

Responsible return, no pressure

Measure learning, renewal, or referral return while auditing for complaints, unwanted reminders, and privacy leakage.

Resilience

Critical edge cases and recovery paths

Beneficiary declines

Response: close the invitation privately, stop reminders, do not collect registration data, and apply the approved cancellation/refund rule if money was already sent.

Sponsor assists too early

Response: block data entry until the beneficiary receives the notice and records agreement; remind both parties that assistance does not transfer decision-making.

Invalid or shared referral link

Response: load the general landing page without attribution, explain the issue, and allow legitimacy verification; never guess the intended sponsor.

Form fails on weak connectivity

Response: preserve unsent values locally, show a plain-language retry, prevent duplicates, and offer an approved offline or in-person route.

Payment succeeds but callback fails

Response: remain “pending verification,” retain the official reference, avoid a second charge, and reconcile with PRC before marking paid.

Payment made with wrong reference

Response: do not manually reassign without authorization; create a tracked PRC payment escalation and keep both users informed at a high level.

PRC rejects or requests correction

Response: use “needs attention,” state the next action without exposing internal notes to the sponsor, and send the beneficiary through an approved correction path.

Privacy approval is incomplete

Response: run the pilot using synthetic/test data only. Real applicant intake remains disabled until the privacy gate is formally cleared.

Content becomes stale

Response: expire or unpublish the affected claim, direct users to PRC, obtain a new review/approval, and preserve the audit history.

Emergency or claims question

Response: show Hotline 143 and official PRC claims routes. The project admin may help the user find the route but must not decide eligibility or outcome.

Pilot scorecard

Measures attached to the journey

≥80%Understanding

Users answer at least four of five comprehension questions correctly after the learning flow.

<5 minSponsor effort

Median sponsor setup time, excluding external payment or official processing.

<10 minBeneficiary effort

Median education, agreement, and intake time, excluding official processing.

100%Agreement evidence

Completed intake records include approved agreement evidence or documented lawful basis.

≥95%Reliable actions

Platform actions complete without unhandled error; failure always exposes a recovery path.

30Verified memberships

Proposed school-pilot target after baselines and PRC processing assumptions are confirmed.

0Unsupported claims

No known unapproved benefit, eligibility, timing, or integration claims at launch.

0Public recipient exposure

No public beneficiary identities, health/claims data, or recipient-ranking mechanics.

Governance note

This journey is an internal design and planning artifact. It does not authorize collection of real applicant data, payment processing, use of PRC identity, or public claims about benefits. Every production change requires PRC approval. Detailed claims and exclusions must be replaced or confirmed against controlling PRC terms before release.
